data.content_ref: inline:SRC_004 frames the panel-vs-expert comparison as a product of (theory quality, execution fidelity) and claims aggregation is not a separate factor. But this is refuted by a basic Condorcet mechanism: if N non-expert executors each have error rate p<1/2 *independently*, majority-vote reliability approaches 1 as N grows, even holding theory quality and individual execution fidelity fixed. This aggregation boost is neither a theory-quality improvement nor a per-executor fidelity improvement; it is a structural property of the voting layer under independence. SRC_004's own refutation condition names exactly this ('a reliability boost not factorizable into either theory quality or execution fidelity'), yet the Condorcet result shows that condition is satisfied, so the claimed 'dissolves into product' framing fails for the panel case specifically.
